Analysis by Richard Cowan

Over the years that I have been doing MarijuanaNews.com, I have tried to stay “on topic”

-- focusing on just cannabis as far as possible. Of course the very real war on cannabis

takes place in the context of the phony “War on Drugs” – which takes place in the context

of the seriously malfunctioning “criminal justice system” – which operates in the context of

the general mess made by the appalling people who govern us. Occasionally, I have

digressed to write about the changing context.

See

Baghdad on The Bayou. Chernobyl for the American Political Class. Changing the

Context for the Drugwar. How Damaging This Fiasco Must Be To The Morale Of Our

Troops In Iraq.

and

The Editors Of The Washington Post Should Read This Book Review. Well, Obviously

They Have, But Just Didn’t Understand It. The Context For Marijuana Prohibition.

I have never made a secret of the fact that I am a libertarian, but I have never had any

illusions about libertarianism being other than a minority view that was often marginal in

its immediate impact on events.

On the other hand, “Libertarianism” as a political philosophy has a much greater political

impact. For example, the Cato Institute in Washington is a major source of ideas for very

non-libertarian Conservatives who treat it like an intellectual buffet, where they can pick

and choose which ideas will they will use to justify the legislation that they support.

However, at least they are exposed to other ideas, like ending the drug war. Gasp!

Their limitations aren’t Cato’s fault, and Cato is always candid about its commitment to its

libertarian principles. Moreover, many of the brightest staffers working for the

Conservative Republicans are really closet libertarians.

The Libertarian Party on the other hand, really is marginal in its impact.

Which brings us to Ron Paul…

The “Ron Paul phenomenon” is the result of a number of factors, Ron Paul’s personality

being the least of them. Paul is intelligent, sincere and committed, but –

most importantly

– this year he is “None of the Above” when the American people are fed up with the two

major parties.

George Bush has even alienated the Republican base, and the Democratic Party leadership

is a huge disappointment to the anti-war Progressives, who would like to think of

themselves as their base. (Actually, the Dems’ base is broader. It is also the government

employee unions, and the very badly led African-Americans.)

None of the major candidates will ever say anything about the Drug War, or even medical

marijuana, unless absolutely forced to do so (and then it is usually something stupid),

which is where “None of the Above” comes in – or should.

In the last two Presidential elections the Libertarian Presidential candidates got around

400,000 votes, which is less than half the number of Americans who were arrested on

marijuana charges last year. (Note: most of them did not lose their right to vote.)

Nonetheless, even the candidates for the LP Presidential nominations – with the exception

of Steve Kubby –only pay lip service to their opposition to the dug war or even to

marijuana prohibition. “Of course, I oppose…”

And that is especially true of Ron Paul.

But, as I said earlier, the war on cannabis and the Drug War in general, are a part of a

much bigger – global– problem with “law enforcement.” Most of the world’s criminal

justice systems are corrupt politically and financially. They are essentially instruments of

state oppression and systematic graft.

And they are the only part of government which most people encounter on a regular basis.

That is as true in America as it is in Mexico or Zimbabwe. Consequently, any candidate

who wants to have an impact on the everyday lives of real people must address the

problems with the mechanisms of state violence.

The Libertarians may or may not be able to elect the next President of the US, but they

should at least insist that the issue that affects the most people be on the public agenda.

For example, if I had to make a short list of the most influential politicians of the 20th

Century it would certainly include someone that most people have never heard of –

Norman Thomas, the perennial Socialist Party Presidential candidate.

He never came close to getting elected, but many of the policies which advocated became

law.

This is why I am backing Steve Kubby’s very long-shot Presidential bid. Steve is the one

candidate who has fought the system on the front lines. He did not exactly win the battle,

but he survived to fight another day, and did not just run off and hide.

See

Kubby to Return to Jail. Survival Depends on Marinol. Two and Half Years Probation to

Follow. Triumph of Prosecutorial State. Special to MarijuanaNews.

He knows all too well the dangers of “law enforcement” that will not obey the law, and he

knows all too well that most people do not have the resources and support to fight the

omnipotent state.

See

Selective Enforcement Versus Selective Compliance – 2 Articles

That is why Steve Kubby is the real “law and order” candidate.

See

It’s The Stupidity, Stupid. How the Prohibitionist Ideology Has Wrecked The Republican

Party and Undermined Democracy Everywhere. When Ideology Trumps Reality, The

Result is Stupidity.

If the Libertarian Party is ever to become a real factor in American politics, it is going to

have to earn the trust of the people by standing up for their rights on the front lines, and

stop showing up every four years to see if self-evident truth has triumphed for them.

That is why Steve and I have started a new project on BlogTalkRadio.com, which is

subtitled “Leading from the Front Lines” – which is what Steve is trying to do. This is also

what the LP must do to have any real impact in the next election and beyond.

Dwight Eisenhower said, “Pull the string, and it will follow wherever you wish. Push it, and

it will go nowhere at all.”

In the real world leading often means pulling. Just standing up and speaking truth to

power is important and often courageous, but if Power doesn’t have to listen, it does not

matter what you say. And if the people think that you are not talking for them, they are not

going to listen to what you are saying to them.

The Internet is offering us many ways to communicate with one another… or just to shout

in the wind. It is up to us who care about cannabis to communicate with those who say they

care about freedom. Join us!

See

Richard Cowan to Host The Steve Kubby Show On Blogtalkradio.com Starting Wednesday
